ledger.claim: POL-NS-01 is conjunctive and its limb (a) fails on the face of the record: the trip_record carries no driver 'arrived' event at all. arrived_at is null and the event list holds only driver_assigned, driver_en_route and trip_cancelled. A no-show fee cannot be charged where the platform's own telemetry never records the arrival that limb (a) requires, and breaking this single limb is enough to defeat the charge.

Limb (d) of POL-NS-01 fails as well. The trip is recorded under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CANCELLED with cancelled_by RIDER — not RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT — and it was terminated by the rider, not by the driver. Limb (d) requires the driver's termination on one of those three codes at or after the required dwell; none of that is present, so the fee is not chargeable under the anchor clause.

POL-NS-02 puts the driver nowhere near the pickup point. Across 49 fixes his nearest approach to the pin was 7,000.01 m and his farthest 15,000.05 m, and the trace yields 0 qualifying in-radius fixes — the arrival radius for this STANDARD zone class being 50 m. With no qualifying in-radius fix in the 15 minutes preceding cancellation, the driver never arrived, limb (b) of POL-NS-01 fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the cancellation fee.

POL-NS-03 cannot rescue the fee either. Its whole test is a driver stationary outside the arrival radius but not more than 400 m from the pickup pin. The closest this driver came was 7,000.01 m — more than seventeen times that ceiling — so this is not a wrong-entrance or wrong-block case, no fault allocation arises and no pin-ambiguity goodwill is engaged.

POL-NS-10 is the clause that decides a fee the rider's own cancellation triggered, and its limb (f) exception applies squarely. The rider cancelled at 21:44:13, 420 seconds after the 21:37:13 acceptance and so beyond the 180 second grace, but the chat log shows the driver asked her to cancel: MSG-02757-001, sent 21:41:13, reads 'sorry got a problem with the car, can you cancel on your side', and she answered 'ok cancelling' at 21:42:13. Where the record shows the driver asked the rider to cancel, limb (f) directs that the fee be refunded in full.

POL-NS-06 is drafted as strict liability and the arithmetic is one-sided: the effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds against the free waiting period of 180 seconds in force for this trip (platform_policy.free_wait_sec), a shortfall of 180 seconds. On a shortfall the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she responded to messages. The waiting period is the consideration the fee was paid for, and this driver never began to earn it.

I disclose the impairment on which this claim rests: EV-ADVIS-02757-01 is MISSING, carries no payload and bears weight_multiplier 0.0 on issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. No advisory covers Blk 12 Telok Blangah Cres in this window, and that absence is itself citable. It makes POL-NS-06(i)'s accumulation limb unavailable — there is no KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT advisory that could permit separate in-geofence intervals to be summed — and in any event the trace shows 0 in-geofence intervals to sum and an accumulated dwell of 0.0 seconds. The absence costs the driver any excuse and costs the rider nothing.

Nothing is payable to the driver and nothing may be netted against the rider's refund. POL-NS-07 compensates the driver at 80 percent of the fee only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it; here limbs (a), (b) and (d) all fail, the driver never entered the arrival radius, and POL-NS-06 independently displaces the charge. The 4.50 collected at 21:44:30 is therefore refundable in full with no driver_compensation_sgd alongside it.

The amount in issue and the remedy are fixed by the ledger: total_charged is 4.50, payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, matching the 4.50 cancellation_fee line. The relief the rider seeks is FULL_REFUND, which POL-GEN-03 defines as the filing party being entirely right and the whole contested amount being returned — here the whole 4.50.

The rider was at the pickup point, not absent. Her device's only fix in the trace places her 16.57 m from the pin, inside the 100 m rider-presence radius that POL-NS-04 uses as its STANDARD-zone yardstick, so nothing in the record supports the premise of a rider who failed to appear. The trip ended because the driver asked her to cancel, and her reply came 60 seconds after his message and 2 minutes before she cancelled.

Even if an arrival marker had been pressed, the outcome is the same. No qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in this trip, which is precisely the state POL-NS-05 limb (ii) addresses with a full refund and no compensation; and the trace shows the driver travelling between 57.3 and 63.0 km/h from his first fix to his last, so at no point was he holding position anywhere a waiting clock could start.

This case should be decided now rather than held, so no escalation trigger under POL-NS-09 fires. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming test reads driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d at 2 against driver_profile.completed_trips_30d at 104 — a rate of 0.019, far below the 0.08 limb — rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the 3 that POL-NS-09(d) reads, and both counterparty-dispute counters are 0, so POL-NS-09(c) is not met. The fee should be refunded, not frozen.

The rider's cancellation was made 420 seconds after the trip was accepted (accepted_at 21:37:13, cancelled_at 21:44:13), which is far outside the 180-second grace_after_match_sec in force for this trip. Under POL-NS-10(a) the grace does not make the cancellation non-chargeable, and under POL-NS-10(f) a rider's own cancellation after the grace is chargeable at the platform's published cancellation fee whether or not the driver had arrived.

POL-NS-10(f) makes a post-grace rider cancellation chargeable 'whether or not the driver had arrived', so the rider cannot defeat the fee by pointing to the driver's position. Even taking the rider's best case on the trace - 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes and a minimum driver-to-pin distance of 7,000 m - arrival is simply not an element of the limb (f) charge, and POL-NS-01's arrival and dwell limbs are not the operative test for a cancellation the rider herself initiated after the grace.

The first of POL-NS-10(f)'s four exceptions - that the driver had not begun moving toward the pickup within the grace - is not shown on this record. The trip record logs driver_en_route at 21:37:21, eight seconds after assignment and well inside the 180-second grace, and the driver's track runs continuously from 21:37:13 through 21:45:13 with no gap.

The second POL-NS-10(f) exception - that the driver had not arrived within 180 seconds of the first estimated arrival time shown to the rider - is not engaged. The only ETA shown to the rider was 15 minutes from assignment at 21:37:13, that is 21:52:13, and the rider cancelled at 21:44:13, eight minutes before that time. The driver had not exceeded any arrival time shown to the rider, so the exception has no application.

The fourth POL-NS-10(f) exception - that the vehicle or driver did not match the booking - is not shown. The trip record carries vehicle_type RYDE_X for the booking and names DRV-09757 as the assigned driver, and the record contains no statement or log entry asserting a mismatch was ever raised.

The amount the rider contests reconciles to the policy in force, so there is no fare integrity defect under POL-NS-08(d): the fare_breakdown cancellation-fee line is SGD 4.50, equal to platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of SGD 4.50 for this trip, and the gross figure of SGD 6.61 is the other figure POL-NS-08(d) permits that line to carry. Every artifact in the bundle other than the absent traffic advisory is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so the record on which the charge rests is unimpaired.

The driver's concession, stated rather than stretched: the chat log carries a message from the driver at 21:41:13 reading 'sorry got a problem with the car, can you cancel on your side'. On its terms that is a request that the rider cancel, and the driver does not contest that it engages the third POL-NS-10(f) exception. The driver's fee case therefore rests on the three exceptions above being absent, which they are, while the driver acknowledges that POL-NS-10(f) is drafted in the disjunctive so that any single engaged exception is sufficient.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02757 (EV-FARE-02757: cancellation_fee 4.50, total_charged 4.50, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) is refunded to the rider in full.

The charge was raised on a cancellation the rider herself made, so POL-NS-10 governs. She cancelled at 21:44:13, 420 seconds after the 21:37:13 acceptance on the trip record (EV-TRIP-02757), which is outside the 180-second grace_after_match_sec. Standing alone that makes the fee chargeable under POL-NS-10(f) whether or not the driver had arrived, and the driver is right that three of the four exceptions are not engaged: the driver did begin moving toward the pickup at 21:37:21, inside the grace; the only ETA shown was 15 minutes from assignment (21:52:13), and the rider cancelled at 21:44:13, before it; and no driver or vehicle mismatch is recorded.

The third exception is engaged, however, and POL-NS-10(f) is disjunctive — any single exception refunds the fee in full. The chat log EV-CHAT-02757 (weight_multiplier 1.0, no issue codes) records the driver's message MSG-02757-001 sent 21:41:13 — 'sorry got a problem with the car, can you cancel on your side' — which the rider answered 'ok cancelling' at 21:42:13 and then cancelled. That is the driver asking the rider to cancel, on the chat_log, exactly as the exception requires; the driver advocate concedes it.

Independently the driver never arrived, so POL-NS-10(g) — which would let the fee stand despite limb (f) where the driver had arrived and served the free waiting period — cannot apply. The trip record carries no 'arrived' event (arrived_at null; events only driver_assigned, driver_en_route, trip_cancelled), so POL-NS-01 limb (a) fails. The record was closed under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CANCELLED with cancelled_by RIDER, not one of the three no-show codes, so limb (d) fails. The GPS trace EV-GPS-02757 (weight 1.0) yields 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes with a nearest approach of 7,000.01 m against the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, so limb (b) fails under POL-NS-02, and POL-NS-03's 400 m wrong-entrance ceiling is nowhere near met. POL-NS-06 independently refunds: effective in-geofence dwell 0 s against the 180 s free waiting period in force (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec), a 180 s shortfall. The MISSING traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02757-01 (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no fact; it only makes POL-NS-06(i)'s accumulation limb unavailable, and there are no in-geofence intervals to sum in any event.

Driver compensation: none. POL-NS-07 pays the driver only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces the charge; POL-NS-01 fails and POL-NS-06 displaces it. driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2 against completed_trips_30d 104 (rate 0.019), so the anti-farming check does not trip and there is no POL-NS-09 escalation.

Confidence: 0.95. Every artifact carrying the deciding facts — the chat log, the GPS trace, the trip record and the fare breakdown — is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0; the only artifact below 1.0 is the absent advisory at 0.0, which carries no fact. That is above the 0.70 escalation floor.

Referrals: none. No clause produces one — POL-NS-05's false-arrival record is not engaged because no arrival marker was ever pressed, and POL-NS-07's escalation packet is not triggered.

The monetary effect, SGD 4.50, is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold (POL-GEN-05), so this refund is executed automatically. Either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
